currency.changeInProfile: Change your base currency in your profile

conversion.title: These totals are incomplete
conversion.body: No exchange rate is available for {{currencies}}, so those amounts were left out of the sums instead of being counted as {{base}}. The figures you see are lower than reality.
conversion.partialMonths: These months were also computed while a rate was missing and are understated: {{months}}.
conversion.fix: This resolves as soon as the server can fetch the rate.

dashboard.loadFailed: The summary could not be loaded.
dashboard.noCategories: No categorised spending in this period.
dashboard.noMonths: There are no closed months to chart yet. Monthly snapshots are built from your movements.
dashboard.unknownSavings: No income recorded in this period.
dashboard.unknownFund: With no spending recorded there is nothing to measure your liquid assets against.
dashboard.unknownDebt: A monthly snapshot with income is needed.

wealthness.unknownTrend: There is not enough history yet to see a direction.
wealthness.noSnapshots: There are no monthly snapshots yet. They are built from your movements: as soon as you record the first month, this chart starts filling in.
wealthness.footnote: The thresholds above are conventional personal-finance rules of thumb — three to six months of expenses saved, debt below 36% of income — not a calculation derived from your data.

patrimony.title: What you own, minus what you owe
patrimony.noAssetsRatio: With no assets recorded there is nothing to take a share of.
patrimony.liquidNote: A house is wealth, but it will not pay next month's rent.
patrimony.name: Name
patrimony.noAssets: You have not recorded anything yet. An asset is anything you own and can put a value on: a savings account, a flat, an investment. Without them, net worth is just your debt in negative.
patrimony.noDebts: You have no active debts recorded.

assetForm.description: Record the value in the currency it is actually held in. The conversion to {{base}} is computed when it is read, never written over the original amount.
assetForm.name: Name
assetForm.isLiquidNote: You could turn it into cash within days. Only liquid assets count toward the emergency fund. A five-year term deposit is savings, but it is not liquid.
assetForm.errorValue: The value must be a number of zero or more.

experiences.noneBody: A trip, a course, a wedding: something with a date and a budget of its own, separate from your savings goals. They are created from Goals, by marking the goal as an experience.
experiences.itemisedBudgetNote: What your lines add up to
experiences.planCostsMore: The plan costs more than the target: it is a plan with a hole in it.
experiences.planCostsLess: The plan costs less than the target. With a positive sign, it would be a plan with a hole in it.
experiences.planMatches: The plan and the target match exactly.
experiences.linesNote: Each line keeps its original currency; totals are converted to {{base}}.
experiences.noLines: With no lines, this experience's budget is zero and the difference against the target says nothing. Add what you already know it will cost: flights, lodging, food.
experiences.bookedNote: A booked line is already paid: its price will not move. The rest is still exposed to fare changes and to the exchange rate.

budgetForm.description: From the budget for "{{goal}}". Record the amount in the currency you will pay it in; the total is converted to {{base}}.
budgetForm.label: Item
budgetForm.actualNote: Leave it empty until you spend. The estimate is not overwritten: the gap between the two is what improves your next budget.
budgetForm.bookedNote: Paid or reserved, so the price will not move — neither by fares nor by exchange rate.
budgetForm.errorEstimated: The estimate must be a number of zero or more.

profile.title: Your account
profile.phoneNote: Changing the number marks it unverified again.
profile.baseCurrencyNote: Every total is read in this currency. Each movement keeps the currency it actually happened in; the conversion is computed when it is displayed, never written over the original amount.
profile.ratesNote: Rates refresh once a day from the provider configured on the server.
profile.aiNote: The provider that reads your movements for the analysis. The key is validated when you save it, encrypted on the server, and never returned in full.

twoFactor.title: Two-step verification
twoFactor.intro: With this on, your password alone is no longer enough to get in.
twoFactor.appNote: Generates a six-digit code that changes every 30 seconds. It depends on neither signal nor any external provider.
twoFactor.codesRemaining: You have {{count}} unused recovery codes left.
twoFactor.smsNote: No SMS provider is connected yet, so this option cannot send you anything. We keep it visible so you know it exists, not to pretend it works.
twoFactor.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
twoFactor.secretNote: This key is shown only once. After that it stays encrypted on the server and is never shown again.
twoFactor.confirmWithCode: Confirm with the code your app shows
twoFactor.passwordToDisable: Confirm with your password to disable
twoFactor.passwordToRegenerate: Confirm with your password to generate new codes
twoFactor.disableNote: Turning two-step verification off weakens your account, so your password is asked for again: an open, unattended session should not be able to do it alone.
twoFactor.regenerateNote: The previous codes stop working as soon as the new ones are generated.
twoFactor.saveCodesBody: They are shown once and each works once. They are how you get in if you lose your phone — without them, losing the device means losing the account.
twoFactor.codesFileNote: Each one works once. Keep them somewhere other than your phone.

auth.loginBlurb: Everything you record lives on your own server. No bank, no third-party app and nobody else reads your movements.
auth.registerBlurb: Movements, debts, assets and goals in one place, in the currencies they actually happen in. No fees and no bank to connect.
auth.registerSubtitle: You can turn on two-step verification from your profile as soon as you are in.
auth.mfaBlurb: The second step is still missing. Until you confirm the code, this session has access to none of your data — the intermediate step grants no permissions on its own.
auth.mfaSubtitle: The six-digit one your authenticator app shows.
auth.backupSubtitle: Any of the ten you saved when you turned verification on. Each works once.
auth.expiresAfter: . After that you will have to start again.
auth.expired: This attempt expired. Sign in again to start over.
auth.backupHint: If you lost your phone, any of the ten codes you saved will do — one use each.
auth.otherAccount: Go back and sign in with another account
auth.errorCodeInvalid: That code is not valid. Check your app and try the next one.
auth.errorTokenInvalid: This sign-in attempt expired. Start again.
auth.errorAlreadyEnabled: Two-step verification is already on. Disable it first to enrol another device.

savingsRate.strong: You keep a fifth or more of what you earn.
savingsRate.adequate: You keep between a tenth and a fifth.
savingsRate.low: You keep less than a tenth.
savingsRate.unknown: No income recorded in this period.

emergencyFund.strong: Six months or more of essential spending covered.
emergencyFund.adequate: Between three and six months covered: the usual target.
emergencyFund.low: Under three months. A single setback would hurt.
emergencyFund.unknown: No spending recorded yet to measure against.

debtLoad.high: Above the usual comfort line of 36%.
debtLoad.critical: Above what most lenders will accept.
debtLoad.unknown: A monthly snapshot with income is needed.

trend.net_flow: No assets recorded, so measured on cumulative net flow.
